Proposed definitions (final candidate wording):
- "Capacity Unit (CU)": a unit of reserved capacity equal to one vram-hour on a performance profile equivalent to NVIDIA A100-80GB. For clarity: one CU corresponds to the compute capacity required to serve the defined synthetic workload at p50 latency target on an A100-80GB equivalent device for one hour.
- "CU-hour": one Capacity Unit consumed for one hour. Monthly commitments are measured in CU-hours.
- "Committed CU-hours": the CU-hours the customer has prepaid/reserved for the monthly billing period.
- "Burst Allowance": a short duration allowance permitting the customer to exceed the Committed CU-hours rate by up to 2x for up to 3 hours per calendar day; overage beyond the Burst Allowance will be billed as described in the pricing schedule.
- "Throughput & Latency SLO": Redwood will measure p50 and p95 latency for a defined synthetic workload (seq len 256 chat mix). The p50 latency SLO applies to 95% of the measured samples in the monthly aggregation window.

Service credit ladder (measurement & remedy):
- Measurement window: rolling 5-minute intervals aggregated across the monthly period; incidents are reported with timestamped metrics and RCA within 5 business days.
- Ladder (applies to monthly invoice amount for the committed CU-hours portion):
   * Monthly availability >= 99.9%: 0% credit
   * 99.0% <= availability < 99.9%: 5% credit
   * 95.0% <= availability < 99.0%: 15% credit
   * availability < 95.0%: 30% credit
- Credit cap: aggregate credits for a single monthly billing period are capped at 50% of the monthly committed CU-hours value (negotiable).

Example commit math (worked example):
- Customer target: reserve 4 A100-equivalent devices continuously.
- Monthly CU-hour calculation: 4 CUs * 24 hours * 30 days = 2880 CU-hours/month.
